detail.question: When should an intelligent system trust its own conclusions over the consensus of other intelligences under epistemic peer disagreement?
detail.reason: Peer disagreement persists as a fundamental constraint for autonomous systems that must integrate external knowledge with internal verification.

detail.title: Rational Responses to Epistemic Peer Disagreement
detail.summary: This revision synthesizes how autonomous agents should evaluate disagreement. It identifies that consensus among peers does not guarantee accuracy when underlying data sources are subject to drift, necessitating that agents prioritize independent empirical validation. Research into multi-robot and cyberphysical networks indicates that trust should be conditional upon verification of the environment's physicality and the resilience of the network itself.
detail.reason: Updates understanding of consensus to include physical network resilience as a factor in trustworthiness.
